title: Fundamental theorem of calculus along a segment for a Lipschitz function
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, u : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n) Lipschitz with constant L, and x, y ∈ ℝⁿ. If u is differentiable at (1 − t)y + tx for L¹-almost every t ∈ [0, 1], then u(x) − u(y) = ∫_0^1 Du((1 − t)y + tx)(x − y) dt. Here Du = fderiv ℝ u and the integral is the interval integral from 0 to 1.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (u : Euclid n → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (x y : Euclid n), LipschitzWith L u → (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)), DifferentiableAt ℝ u ((1 - t) • y + t • x)) → u x - u y = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, fderiv ℝ u ((1 - t) • y + t • x) (x - y)
